title: Parameter map
description: Definitions-only. Shapes for the input and output parameter maps an instruction contract declares. $ref-ed by the instruction contract, the program wrapper, and caller-input validation, so none of them has to import another to get the shape.

outputParameter.title: Output parameter
outputParameter.description: One named output an instruction produces. Named even when there is only one, because ${node_id.name} resolves against these names.

type.description: Fixed vocabulary. Composite structure is object or array plus prose in description; runtime shape enforcement is data.validate_schema's job, not the contract's.

inputParameter.title: Input parameter
inputParameter.description: One named input an instruction accepts. Separate from outputParameter so that only an input can declare a default.

type.description: Fixed vocabulary. Composite structure is object or array plus prose in description; runtime shape enforcement is data.validate_schema's job, not the contract's.

required.description: Whether the caller must supply this input. Omitted means true.

default.description: Value used when the caller omits this input. Only meaningful on an optional input, so declaring it obliges the author to state required: false explicitly.
A default is only meaningful on an optional input. required must be present and false — stated outright rather than left to the interaction of two defaults.

inputMap.title: Input map
inputMap.description: The inputs an instruction accepts, keyed by parameter name. May be empty, which states outright that the instruction takes nothing.

propertyNames.description: Parameter names are tokens in path expressions such as ${node_id.result}, so a name carrying . or [ would make the resolver grammar ambiguous. Same pattern as an opcode segment.

outputMap.title: Output map
outputMap.description: The outputs an instruction produces, keyed by parameter name. May be empty.
